Simulate responses from a fitted ZISAR model

Source: R/methods.R
simulate.zisar.Rd

Draws new count vectors from the fitted model, for example for a parametric bootstrap. Each draw takes new random effects \(u\) (and a new inflation field, \(g\) or \(\alpha\), when the model has one), new structural-zero indicators and new negative binomial counts, at the estimated parameters and the observed covariates.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted "zisar" object.

nsim

Number of response vectors to simulate.

seed

Optional seed, passed to set.seed().

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame with nsim columns, one simulated response vector each.

Details

To check a large gradient at the optimum (see zisar()), refit the model to a few simulated responses: if the refits show the same gradient while recovering the parameters, it belongs to the model and not to a spurious optimum. For bootstrap standard errors, start each refit from the estimates with start.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(10, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
ys <- simulate(fit, nsim = 100, seed = 2)
# Share of zeros: observed against simulated
c(observed = mean(sim$data$y == 0), simulated = mean(as.matrix(ys) == 0))
#>  observed simulated 
#>    0.3500    0.3528
